answer: Each agent must lock a deposit before it can trade, and its reputation grows only when randomly selected peers verify completed work against later outcomes. If an audit catches fabricated results or collusion, the agent is slashed and the auditors lose influence if their claims are false. A Sybil swarm therefore needs capital for every account and risks repeated losses; copying names is cheap, but buying durable trust is not, whether the market is a haven, meadow, or ocean.
